purpose.reader_question: How can shared capacity fix the combined labour while allowing different task allocations and schedules?
purpose.expected_reading: The separate square contains impossible pairs, the joint diagonal has fixed sum one, and the marked midpoint has an explicit one-activity-at-a-time schedule.
purpose.claim: For this constructed saturated one-person example, separate bounds sum to [0,2] first-hour person-hours, joint constraints give exactly one, and consecutive full-attention blocks attain P=(1/2,1/2).
purpose.scope: One person, two tasks each totalling one person-hour over [0,2] hours, target [0,1]. Fractional cell totals and full-attention schedules with arbitrary interruption are permitted.
permitted_inferences: Membership in the specified sets of first-hour totals.
Shared capacity can improve combined labour bounds without additional observations.
The marked point has the particular illustrated attaining schedule; this does not identify the actual work history.
prohibited_inferences: A measured workplace result or causal effect of AI.
A probability distribution or statistical confidence interval.
Shared capacity always point-identifies aggregate labour.
The marked point uniquely specifies its schedule, or panel (c) is an observed work history.

inputs.source_reference: Constructed two-task example in article/partial-identification.tex Sections 4.1–4.2, at manuscript baseline 38c4ce40b789d4c5420c98ff1d568b39c3b1e798. The midpoint is selected for one illustrative full-attention schedule.
Exact rational calculation and independent allocation reconstruction in calculate.py; deterministic derived sets, no empirical measurements.
Proposed caption states the constructed inputs, quantities, deterministic feasible sets and scope.
Accessible description of the two plotted projections and their limitations.

quantities.label: Task A first-hour labour
quantities.definition: Person-hours spent on Task A in [0,1]; the full [0,2] task total is one person-hour.
quantities.transformation: Integrate each task allocation in the first hour; sum for combined labour. Values and endpoints are derived with rational arithmetic.

missingness.treatment: This is an exact constructed example, not a sampled or partially observed dataset.

uncertainty.definition: Deterministic permitted values: each component is in [0,1]; adding separate bounds yields [0,2], while enforcing both capacity constraints yields the singleton {1}. No probability coverage is assigned.

quantities.label: Elapsed time in the illustrated schedule
quantities.definition: Elapsed time from the start of the two-hour observation interval.
quantities.transformation: Construct consecutive full-attention task blocks from the derived midpoint cell totals; lengths equal person-hours because one person works at rate one.

uncertainty.definition: The drawn intervals are exact rational constructions; the actual history remains unidentified.

constructions.definition: 0 <= x <= 1 and 0 <= y <= 1, all boundaries included. This is the Cartesian product of separately calculated task bounds, not the joint feasible set.
constructions.method: Apply the one-person interval bound separately to each task total.

constructions.definition: The square intersected with x+y <= 1 and (1-x)+(1-y) <= 1; equivalently x+y=1. Closed endpoints (0,1),(1,0).
constructions.method: First-hour capacity supplies the upper half-plane; second-hour remaining labour supplies the lower half-plane. Construct piecewise-constant feasible allocations for every point of the line.

constructions.definition: Map (x,y) to x+y: the square projects onto [0,2] and the joint line onto {1}. These are deterministic images of sets of interval totals.
constructions.method: Linear projection; rational endpoints from calculate.py.

constructions.definition: P=(1/2,1/2). A occupies [0,1/2) and [1,3/2); B occupies [1/2,1) and [3/2,2], with the final endpoint following B. Each task totals one person-hour, including half a person-hour before time one.
constructions.method: In each one-hour cell, place the A mass then the B mass in consecutive full-attention blocks. Exact overlap integration verifies the first-hour and whole-interval totals.
